name: Step-Up
doThisNotThat: Drive through the top foot only. Pushing off the bottom foot makes it easy and useless.
steps: Box at knee height or a bit lower.
Whole foot on the box, DBs at sides.
Lean slightly forward, stand up using the top leg.
Lower 3 s back down.
homeSwap: Already home: a stair or chair.
note: Lower slowly: the eccentric on a step-up is the knee-protecting part for landing from jumps.

name: Lateral Step-Up
doThisNotThat: Stand side-on and keep the working knee over the second toe. The inside knee collapse is what you are training out.
steps: Stand beside a box with one foot on top.
Push through the top foot to stand.
Lower the other foot to tap the floor slowly.
homeSwap: Already home: stair, side-on.
note: Directly fights the knee-cave part of your flat-foot cascade.

name: Skater Squat
doThisNotThat: Back knee touches a pad behind you; arms reach forward for balance. Diving forward to cheat depth misses the quads.
steps: Stand on one leg, other knee bent behind you.
Arms forward.
Lower until the back knee touches a pad or folded towel.
Stand up through the front foot.
cues: Reach your arms to the wall.
homeSwap: Already home.
note: Great single-leg strength test: your goal is 5 clean reps each leg with no hand assist.

name: Pistol Squat
doThisNotThat: Hold a light DB forward as a counterweight. It makes depth easier and teaches control.
steps: Stand on one leg, other leg forward.
Arms or a light DB out front.
Sit down slowly as low as you control.
Stand up without bouncing.
homeSwap: Already home: start with pistols to a chair.
note: Your stiff ankles will limit depth: put the heel on a book until dorsiflexion improves.

name: Cossack Squat
doThisNotThat: The straight leg toes point up and the squatting heel stays down. Go only as deep as your heel stays flat.
steps: Very wide stance.
Shift to one side and sit down, other leg straight, toes up.
Counterweight DB held in front.
Push back to center and switch.
homeSwap: Already home.
note: Loaded mobility for your stiff adductors and ankles: one of the best for the lateral range needed in wrestling and tennis.

name: Lying Leg Curl
doThisNotThat: Press your hips into the pad so they do not rise, and lower slowly. Hips popping up shortens the hamstrings and kills the stretch.
steps: Kneecaps just off the end of the pad, ankle pad just above the heels.
Hips pressed down, grip the handles.
Curl to full flexion.
Lower 3 s to full extension.
cues: Pull your heels to your glutes.
Push your hips through the pad.
homeSwap: Sliding hamstring curl on socks/towel on a hard floor (hips up), or Nordic curl with feet hooked under a couch.
note: Seated leg curls grew hamstrings more than lying ones (Maeo 2021) because the hip is flexed and the hamstrings are longer. If both are available, prefer seated.

name: Seated Leg Curl
doThisNotThat: Lean your torso forward against the thigh pad. More hip flexion = more hamstring stretch = more growth.
steps: Knees lined up with the machine pivot.
Thigh pad locked down tight.
Lean the torso forward.
Curl to full flexion, lower 3 s.
cues: Pull your heels under the seat.
Lean your chest toward your knees.
homeSwap: Sliding hamstring curl on socks/towel on a hard floor (hips up), or Nordic curl with feet hooked under a couch.
note: Seated leg curls grew the hamstrings more than lying leg curls in Maeo 2021, due to the long hamstring position. Last set: lengthened partials in the top half.

name: Standing Leg Curl
doThisNotThat: Keep the hips square and still; rotating to finish the curl uses your back.
steps: Thigh against the pad, ankle pad above the heel.
Hips square, hold the handles.
Curl fully, lower 3 s.
cues: Pull your heel to your butt.
homeSwap: Sliding hamstring curl on socks/towel on a hard floor (hips up), or Nordic curl with feet hooked under a couch.
note: Each leg separate: shows imbalances common in sprinters. Match reps on both sides.

name: Single-Leg Leg Curl
doThisNotThat: Same machine, one leg at a time, lower slower than you lift.
steps: Same setup as the two-leg curl.
One leg in.
Curl fully, lower 3-4 s.
homeSwap: Sliding hamstring curl on socks/towel on a hard floor (hips up), or Nordic curl with feet hooked under a couch.
note: One leg at a time lets you lower a weight you can only lift with two legs (two-up, one-down eccentric overload).

name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
doThisNotThat: Fight the fall the whole way with hips straight. Breaking at the hips makes it easier and less protective.
steps: Kneel on a pad, ankles anchored under a couch or held by a partner.
Body straight from knees to head, glutes tight.
Lower as slowly as possible.
Catch yourself with your hands, push back up.
cues: Keep a straight line from knees to head.
Fall as slowly as you can.
homeSwap: Already home: anchor feet under the couch.
note: Programs including Nordics reduced hamstring injuries by up to about 51% (van Dyk 2019; a later reappraisal is less certain). 2 × 4-6, 1-2x a week is enough.

name: Slider Hamstring Curl
doThisNotThat: Keep the hips up the whole set. Hips dropping turns it into a sloppy bridge.
steps: Lie on your back, heels on sliders or a towel on a smooth floor.
Bridge your hips up.
Slide heels out slowly 3 s, hips stay up.
Pull heels back to your glutes.
cues: Pull your heels to your glutes.
Push your hips to the ceiling.
homeSwap: Already home: socks on a hard floor.
note: Best home hamstring curl. Make it single-leg once 12 two-leg reps is easy.

name: Stability Ball Leg Curl
doThisNotThat: Hips stay up as the ball rolls in. Hips sagging puts it all on the back.
steps: Lie on your back, heels on the ball.
Bridge up.
Curl the ball in, hips high.
Roll out 3 s.
cues: Pull the ball to your butt.
homeSwap: Sliding hamstring curl on socks/towel on a hard floor (hips up), or Nordic curl with feet hooked under a couch.
note: The unstable ball also trains the small ankle muscles your flat feet need.

name: Glute-Ham Raise
doThisNotThat: Knees just behind the pad; lower to horizontal under control and curl up using the hamstrings, not by hinging.
steps: Feet on the plate, knees just behind the pad.
Body straight.
Lower to horizontal.
Curl back up with hamstrings.
cues: Pull yourself up with your heels.
Straight line from knees to head.
homeSwap: Nordic hamstring curl with feet under a couch.
note: Trains hamstrings at both the knee and hip, like they work in a sprint.

name: Leg Extension
doThisNotThat: Lean back slightly or recline the seat. A more open hip lengthens the rectus femoris and makes the quads work harder.
steps: Knee joint lined up with the machine pivot.
Ankle pad just above the ankle.
Grip the handles, lean back slightly.
Extend to straight, lower 3 s to full bend.
cues: Kick the pad to the ceiling.
homeSwap: Sissy squat holding a door frame, or a heels-elevated goblet squat on 2 plates/books, knees driving far past toes.
note: Reclining lengthens the rectus femoris (it crosses the hip), which should load it harder; that is mechanism-based. Last set: lengthened partials in the bottom half.

name: Single-Leg Leg Extension
doThisNotThat: One leg at a time to fix imbalances; same slow lowering.
steps: Same setup as the two-leg extension.
One leg.
Extend fully, lower 3 s.
homeSwap: Sissy squat holding a door frame, or a heels-elevated goblet squat on 2 plates/books, knees driving far past toes.
note: Quads are often weaker on the side that collapses most (often the flatter foot); start with that leg.

name: Reverse Nordic
doThisNotThat: Hips stay extended and body straight from knees to head as you lean back. Bending at the hips removes the stretch.
steps: Kneel on a pad, toes tucked or flat.
Squeeze glutes, body straight.
Lean back slowly as far as you control.
Pull back up with the quads.
cues: Straight line from knees to head.
homeSwap: Already home.
note: Loads the quads and hip flexors at length; great for your stiff hip flexors and knee health in deceleration.

name: Spanish Squat
doThisNotThat: Sit back into the band with shins vertical and hold. It loads the quads with little knee shear.
steps: Loop a heavy band around a post and behind both knees.
Step back until the band is tight.
Sit down with vertical shins, torso upright.
Hold 30-45 s.
cues: Push your knees back into the band.
homeSwap: Wall sit at about 70-90° knee bend, 30-45 s holds.
note: Isometric holds can calm down patellar tendon pain; useful after lots of jumping. Five 45 s holds is a common dose (grade C).

name: Terminal Knee Extension
doThisNotThat: Lock the knee fully against the band. Most of the benefit is in the last 10-20°.
steps: Band around the back of the knee, anchored in front.
Step back until tight.
Let the knee bend 20-30°.
Straighten fully and squeeze 1 s.
cues: Push the back of your knee into the band.
homeSwap: Single-leg wall sit or straight-leg raise, 1 s squeeze at the top.
note: Rehab and warm-up tool. Pair with the Screw cue to line up knee and foot before squats.

name: Wall Sit
doThisNotThat: Thighs parallel, shins vertical, push through the heels. Hands off the thighs.
steps: Back against a wall.
Slide down until thighs are parallel.
Shins vertical, feet flat.
Hold.
cues: Push the wall up with your back.
homeSwap: Already home.
note: Isometric holds are a good knee-friendly way to train quads the day before a game.

name: Standing Calf Raise
doThisNotThat: Pause 2 s in the deepest stretch at the bottom. Bouncing out of it uses the tendon, not the muscle.
steps: Balls of the feet on the edge of the step.
Knees straight but not locked.
Lower 2 s to the deepest stretch, pause 2 s.
Rise as high as possible, squeeze 1 s.
cues: Push the platform through the floor.
Rise tall onto your big toe.
homeSwap: Single-leg calf raise off a stair, holding a DB, 2 s pause at the bottom stretch.
note: Lengthened partials (bottom half only) grew the calves more than full reps (Kassiano 2023). Finish every set with them.

name: Seated Calf Raise
doThisNotThat: Same deep 2 s stretch at the bottom. The bent knee shifts work to the soleus.
steps: Knees under the pad, balls of feet on the edge.
Lower 2 s to full stretch, pause.
Rise high, squeeze.
cues: Push the pad up with your toes.
homeSwap: Seated on a chair, heavy DB on each knee, balls of feet on a book.
note: The soleus is the main calf muscle for running; strong soleus = more running economy for XC.

name: Leg Press Calf Raise
doThisNotThat: Keep the knees straight and safety stops on. Let the platform travel all the way into the stretch.
steps: Balls of feet on the bottom edge of the platform.
Knees straight, safeties engaged.
Lower to full stretch, pause 2 s.
Push up high.
cues: Push the platform with your big toes.
homeSwap: Single-leg calf raise off a stair, holding a DB, 2 s pause at the bottom stretch.
note: Easy to load heavy with zero balance demand; finish with lengthened partials.

name: Donkey Calf Raise
doThisNotThat: Hips flexed so the gastrocs are already stretched; go to the deepest stretch and pause.
steps: Hinge forward, hands on a bench.
Balls of feet on a step.
Lower deep, pause 2 s.
Rise high.
homeSwap: Single-leg calf raise off a stair, holding a DB, 2 s pause at the bottom stretch.
note: The hip flexion lengthens the gastrocnemius further, a cheap lengthened-bias calf builder.

name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
doThisNotThat: Rise over the big toe, not rolling out to the little toe. That is your flat foot leaking force sideways.
steps: Stand on one foot on a step, hold a wall.
DB in the same-side hand.
Lower 2 s to the deepest stretch, pause.
Rise high over the big toe.
cues: Push the step down with your big toe.
homeSwap: Already home: stair + DB.
note: Strengthens the arch-supporting muscles (the tibialis posterior works hard here); the best calf and foot exercise for your flat feet.

name: Tibialis Raise
doThisNotThat: Lean your back against a wall with heels forward; the further out the feet, the harder.
steps: Back against a wall, heels 30-60 cm out.
Legs straight.
Pull your toes up to your shins as high as possible.
Lower slowly.
cues: Pull your toes to the ceiling.
homeSwap: Already home.
note: Balances calf work and protects the shins from running load (shin splints are common in XC). Grade C.

name: Barbell Hip Thrust
doThisNotThat: Chin tucked and ribs down at the top. Arching the low back to "finish" moves the work out of the glutes.
steps: Shoulder blades on a bench edge, bar padded over the hips.
Feet flat, shins vertical at the top.
Lower hips 2 s.
Drive up until hips are level with knees, squeeze 1 s.
cues: Drive the bar to the ceiling.
homeSwap: Single-leg hip thrust with shoulders on the couch, DB on the hip, 2 s squeeze at the top.
note: The thrust loads the glutes hardest at full hip extension, the opposite of a squat; doing both covers the whole range. At home, go single-leg to make light DBs hard.

name: Dumbbell Hip Thrust
doThisNotThat: Hold the DB on the hip crease with both hands; pause 2 s at the top.
steps: Upper back on a couch or bench.
DB on the hips.
Lower 2 s, drive up, squeeze 2 s.
homeSwap: Already home.
note: With light DBs, pause at the top and go single-leg to make it hard.

name: Single-Leg Hip Thrust
doThisNotThat: Keep the hips level. One side dropping means the working glute is losing.
steps: Upper back on a bench, one foot planted.
Other knee pulled up.
Lower 2 s, drive up, squeeze.
homeSwap: Already home.
note: Single-leg hip extension is how you sprint and push off; this is the most sport-specific glute builder at home.

name: Hip Thrust Machine
doThisNotThat: Same chin-tucked, ribs-down finish. Machines make it easy to overextend the back.
steps: Back on the pad, belt over the hips.
Feet so shins are vertical at the top.
Drive up, squeeze 1 s, lower 2 s.
cues: Push the belt to the ceiling.
homeSwap: Single-leg hip thrust with shoulders on the couch, DB on the hip, 2 s squeeze at the top.
note: Simple to push close to failure safely: good for the last set of a glute day.

name: Glute Bridge
doThisNotThat: Squeeze the glutes for 2 s at the top with ribs down; fast bounce reps barely work.
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat.
Push through heels, lift hips.
Squeeze 2 s, lower slowly.
cues: Push the floor away with your heels.
homeSwap: Already home.
note: Good warm-up to wake the glutes before sprinting; your arm-first sequencing starts with lazy hips.

name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
doThisNotThat: Hips level; pause at the top.
steps: On your back, one foot planted, other leg straight up or knee hugged.
Lift hips.
Squeeze 2 s, lower slowly.
cues: Push the floor away with your heel.
homeSwap: Already home.
note: Hugging the other knee to the chest stops you from arching the back to cheat.

name: Frog Pump
doThisNotThat: Soles together, knees out, short fast reps with a hard squeeze. It is a pump finisher, not a strength move.
steps: On your back, soles of feet together, knees out.
Heels close to your butt.
Thrust hips up, squeeze.
Repeat fast.
cues: Push your knees to the floor.
homeSwap: Already home.
note: A quick finisher: 2 × 20-30 for a glute pump without fatiguing your legs before sport.

name: Cable Glute Kickback
doThisNotThat: Hinge forward ~45° and kick back and up with a slight bend in the knee. Swinging the leg uses momentum and your back.
steps: Ankle cuff on, low pulley.
Hold the frame, hinge forward 30-45°.
Kick back until the hip is fully extended.
Return slowly.
cues: Kick your heel to the wall behind you.
homeSwap: Quadruped donkey kick with a DB behind the knee.
note: The hinge puts the glute in a longer position at the start, giving more stretch.

name: Glute Kickback Machine
doThisNotThat: Full range and a 1 s squeeze at the top; no low-back arch.
steps: Chest on the pad, foot on the plate.
Kick back to full hip extension.
Squeeze, return slowly.
cues: Push the plate to the ceiling.
homeSwap: Quadruped donkey kick with a DB behind the knee.
note: Good pump finisher after squats or lunges.

name: Hip Abduction Machine
doThisNotThat: Lean your torso forward slightly. It shifts the work to the upper glute, which is the knee-cave fixer.
steps: Sit with knees on the pads.
Lean forward 20-30°.
Push the pads out as far as possible.
Return slowly.
cues: Push the pads to the walls.
homeSwap: Side-lying hip abduction, toes slightly down, 2 s pause at the top.
note: The glute med stops the knee caving inward when your arch collapses; this is the gym version of the Screw cue.

name: Cable Hip Abduction
doThisNotThat: Stand tall and lift the leg out to the side without leaning. Leaning means the weight is too heavy.
steps: Cuff on the outside ankle, low pulley.
Stand side-on, hold the frame.
Lift the leg out 30-45°.
Return slowly.
cues: Push your heel to the wall.
homeSwap: Side-lying hip abduction.
note: The standing leg works too: grip the tripod foot to keep the arch up.

name: Banded Lateral Walk
doThisNotThat: Stay low in a quarter squat and keep tension the whole time; feet never come together.
steps: Band above the knees or around the ankles.
Quarter squat, feet hip width.
Step sideways 10-15 steps each way.
cues: Push your knees out against the band.
homeSwap: Side-lying hip abduction, or lateral shuffles in a quarter squat.
note: Pre-game activation for cutting sports: wakes up the glute med before you change direction.

name: Side-Lying Hip Abduction
doThisNotThat: Keep the top leg slightly behind you with toes pointing down. Bringing it forward turns it into a hip flexor move.
steps: Lie on your side, bottom knee bent.
Top leg straight, slightly behind the body, toes down.
Lift 30-40 cm.
Pause 1 s, lower slowly.
cues: Push your heel to the wall.
homeSwap: Already home.
note: Simple and effective for the knee-cave part of the flat-foot cascade.

name: Copenhagen Plank
doThisNotThat: Start with the bench at the knee (short lever) and work toward the ankle. Jumping straight to the long lever is how groins get tweaked.
steps: Side plank with your top leg on a bench (knee for short lever, ankle for long).
Bottom leg under the bench.
Lift the hips into a straight line.
Hold or do slow reps lifting the bottom leg to the bench.
cues: Push the bench down with your top leg.
homeSwap: Already home: use a couch.
note: One Copenhagen exercise 3x/week preseason then 1x/week was linked to 41% lower odds of groin problems (Harøy 2019).

name: Adduction Machine
doThisNotThat: Set the start as wide as is comfortable and lower slowly. The wide, stretched position is where the growth is.
steps: Sit, knees on the pads, start wide.
Squeeze the pads together.
Return 3 s to the widest position.
homeSwap: Copenhagen plank, or lying adduction with a DB-free side plank.
note: Your adductors are stiff: the wide loaded stretch here improves your squat depth and lateral range.

name: Cable Hip Adduction
doThisNotThat: Stand tall and pull the leg across the body slowly; no swinging.
steps: Cuff on the inside ankle, low pulley.
Stand side-on.
Pull the leg across in front of the standing leg.
Return slowly.
cues: Sweep your foot across the floor.
homeSwap: Copenhagen plank on a couch.
note: Adductor strength helps every lateral push-off in basketball and every shot in wrestling.

name: Landmine Squat
doThisNotThat: Hold the bar end at your chest and lean into it slightly; the arc lets you sit deep and upright.
steps: Bar end in a landmine or corner, hold it at your sternum with both hands.
Feet shoulder width, slightly in front of you.
Sit down 3 s to full depth.
Stand driving the bar up the arc.
homeSwap: Goblet squat with your heaviest DB, 3 s lowering + 1 s pause in the hole, or a 1.5-rep squat (down, half up, down, up).
note: The angled load is forgiving on stiff ankles and hips, so it is a good stepping stone to a full back squat.

name: Overhead Squat
doThisNotThat: Start with a broomstick. Your mobility, not your strength, sets the load here.
steps: Wide snatch grip, bar locked overhead.
Push the bar up and slightly back, armpits forward.
Squat down 3 s keeping the bar over mid-foot.
Stand tall.
cues: Push the bar to the ceiling.
homeSwap: Overhead squat with a broomstick or one light DB held overhead (single-arm).
note: A full-body mobility test for your all-over stiffness: film it monthly; deeper and more upright = progress.

name: Dumbbell Sumo Squat
doThisNotThat: Stand on two boxes or plates so the DB can drop below your feet; more depth = more adductor stretch.
steps: Wide stance, toes out 30-45°.
One DB hanging between your legs by the top head.
Sit straight down 3 s, knees out over the toes.
Stand up squeezing the glutes.
cues: Push your knees out to the walls.
homeSwap: Already home: stand on two stairs or books.
note: Loads your stiff adductors in a long position, which helps squat depth and lateral range.

name: Kettlebell Deadlift
doThisNotThat: Bell between the feet in line with your ankles; hips back and push the floor away.
steps: Bell between your feet, mid-foot line.
Hinge and grip with a flat back.
Push the floor away, stand tall.
Hinge back down with control.
homeSwap: Single-leg DB RDL, 3 s lowering, both DBs in the opposite hand to the working leg.
note: The cleanest way to learn the hinge before a barbell; perfect for home with one heavy DB.

name: Smith Machine Split Squat
doThisNotThat: The bar balances for you, so push close to failure and go deep.
steps: Bar on traps, front foot slightly ahead of the bar line.
Back foot on a bench or floor.
Lower 3 s.
Drive up.
cues: Push the front foot through the floor.
homeSwap: Rear-foot-elevated split squat on a couch or step, DBs at your sides, 3 s lowering.
note: Removes balance so you can load single-leg hard; mix with free versions for athletic transfer.

name: Landmine Reverse Lunge
doThisNotThat: Hold the bar end in the hand opposite the working leg; it challenges hip stability like a punch from a split stance.
steps: Bar end held at the shoulder or hip.
Step back into a lunge.
Lower 2-3 s.
Drive back up through the front foot.
cues: Push the front foot through the floor.
homeSwap: DB reverse lunge with the DB in the opposite hand.
note: Offset load builds the anti-rotation core you need to stay stable while throwing punches from a staggered stance.

name: Step-Down
doThisNotThat: Lower the free heel to the floor in 3 s with the knee over the second toe; do not drop.
steps: Stand on a step on one leg.
Slowly lower the free heel toward the floor.
Tap lightly, stand back up.
cues: Tap the floor like it is hot.
homeSwap: Already home: a stair.
note: Controlled knee bend on one leg is exactly the landing skill that protects your knees in jumps and cuts.

name: Poliquin Step-Up
doThisNotThat: Heel on a raised plate, knee drives forward over the toes and you push up through the front of the foot. Small range, high quality.
steps: Stand on a low step with the working heel raised on a small plate.
Lower the other heel toward the floor, knee forward.
Push back up through the forefoot.
cues: Push your knee over your toes.
homeSwap: Already home: a book under the heel on a stair.
note: Knee-forward strength for the VMO, a classic knee-health drill for jumping athletes.

name: Hip Airplane
doThisNotThat: Rotate the hip open and closed while keeping the standing foot arched. Hold a wall at first.
steps: Stand on one leg, hinge until your torso is near parallel.
Rotate your pelvis open toward the ceiling slowly.
Rotate back closed.
Keep the standing knee over the toes.
cues: Turn your belly button to the wall.
Grip the floor with your foot.
homeSwap: Already home.
note: Trains the hip rotation control your flat-foot cascade throws off; great before cutting sports.

name: Kas Glute Bridge
doThisNotThat: Only move the top third of a hip thrust, keeping chin tucked and ribs down. Constant glute tension.
steps: Hip thrust setup.
Lift to full extension.
Lower only a few inches, then thrust back up.
cues: Drive the bar to the ceiling.
homeSwap: Single-leg hip thrust with shoulders on the couch, DB on the hip, 2 s squeeze at the top.
note: Short range at the top where glutes are shortest: good pump finisher after a full-range hinge.

name: Kneeling Leg Curl
doThisNotThat: Keep the hip still and lower slowly; the hip-flexed position gives more hamstring stretch than lying.
steps: Kneel on the pad, forearms supported.
Working ankle under the roller.
Curl, lower 3 s.
cues: Pull your heel to your butt.
homeSwap: Sliding hamstring curl on socks/towel on a hard floor (hips up), or Nordic curl with feet hooked under a couch.
note: Hip flexion lengthens the hamstrings, which should load them harder at the start of the rep (mechanism-based).

name: Bodyweight Calf Raise
doThisNotThat: Go off a stair for the full stretch, pause at the bottom.
steps: Balls of feet on a stair, hold the rail.
Lower 2 s, pause 2 s.
Rise high, squeeze 1 s.
cues: Push the stair down with your big toes.
homeSwap: Already home.
note: Once 25 reps is easy, go single-leg: your flat feet benefit most from the single-leg version.

name: Smith Machine Calf Raise
doThisNotThat: Stand on a plate or step for the deep stretch, pause at the bottom.
steps: Bar on traps, balls of feet on a step.
Lower 2 s, pause.
Rise high.
cues: Push the step down with your big toes.
homeSwap: Single-leg calf raise off a stair, holding a DB, 2 s pause at the bottom stretch.
note: Finish each set with bottom-half lengthened partials (Kassiano 2023).

name: Single-Leg Hip Hinge Bodyweight
doThisNotThat: Reach both hands to the floor slowly with hips square; balance is the training.
steps: Stand on one leg, soft knee.
Hinge forward as the back leg rises.
Reach toward the floor 3 s.
Return tall.
cues: Reach your back heel to the wall.
homeSwap: Already home.
note: Daily balance and foot drill: do it barefoot to train the tripod foot.

name: Dumbbell Step-Up to Knee Drive
doThisNotThat: Drive up and snap the opposite knee to hip height, like a sprint stride.
steps: Foot on a knee-height box.
Push through the top foot.
Drive the other knee up fast at the top.
Lower 3 s.
cues: Punch your knee to the ceiling.
homeSwap: Already home: stair step-up with knee drive.
note: Matches the sprint and jump pattern: hip extension on one side, knee drive on the other.

name: Pull-Up
doThisNotThat: Start every rep from a dead hang with shoulders set down, not a half-rep from bent arms with shrugged shoulders.
steps: Grip the bar overhand just outside shoulder width, thumbs around the bar.
Hang with arms long, then pull the shoulder blades down 1-2 inches without bending the elbows.
Squeeze legs together, toes slightly in front, ribs down.
Pull until the chin clears the bar, then lower in 2-3 s to a full hang.
cues: Pull the bar down to your chest
Drive your elbows into your back pockets
homeSwap: Dumbbell pullover on the floor (lengthened lats) + one-arm DB row with the elbow driving toward the hip to bias lats.
note: Lats are the "V" of the V-taper and the engine of the clinch frame and the double-leg finish; a full dead hang every rep also lengthens a stiff upper back and shoulders.
hardestPoint: Top 3 inches, where the lats are short and the biceps take over.

name: Wide-Grip Pull-Up
doThisNotThat: Go only ~1.5x shoulder width, not as wide as the bar allows; super-wide grips shorten range and strain the shoulder.
steps: Grip about 1.5x shoulder width overhand.
Set the shoulders down from a dead hang.
Pull the upper chest toward the bar, slight lean back.
Lower in 2-3 s to full hang.
cues: Bring your chest to the bar
Bend the bar into a U
homeSwap: Dumbbell pullover on the floor (lengthened lats) + one-arm DB row with the elbow driving toward the hip to bias lats.
note: Wide grip biases the upper lats and teres major that make the back look wider from the front; keep reps fewer and cleaner than standard pull-ups.

name: Neutral-Grip Pull-Up
doThisNotThat: Use neutral grip if your shoulders or elbows complain on overhand; it is the most joint-friendly vertical pull.
steps: Grab the parallel handles, palms facing each other.
Dead hang, shoulders pulled down.
Pull until the chin passes the handles, elbows tight to the ribs.
Lower in 2-3 s.
cues: Pull your elbows down to your hips
Lift your chest to your hands
homeSwap: Dumbbell pullover on the floor (lengthened lats) + one-arm DB row with the elbow driving toward the hip to bias lats.
note: Neutral grip matches the hand position of a clinch frame and a grappling collar tie, so the strength carries straight over.

name: Weighted Pull-Up
doThisNotThat: Add weight only once you own 8+ strict bodyweight reps; ugly kipping with a plate is not strength.
steps: Hold a dumbbell between your feet or hang a plate from a dip belt.
Dead hang, shoulders set down, legs still.
Pull chin over the bar without swinging.
Lower in 2-3 s; stop the set when a rep visibly slows.
cues: Pull the bar to your collarbones
Keep the weight still under you
homeSwap: Dumbbell pullover on the floor (lengthened lats) + one-arm DB row with the elbow driving toward the hip to bias lats.
note: At ~130 lb your relative strength is the athletic number; +10-25 lb for sets of 4-6 is plenty to drive the lats without grinding.

name: Assisted Pull-Up Machine
doThisNotThat: Use the least assistance that still lets you hit full range; lower the counterweight a notch every week you hit the top of the rep range.
steps: Set the counterweight (more weight = more help).
Kneel or stand on the pad, grip just outside shoulder width.
Start from straight arms with shoulders set down.
Pull chin over the handles, lower in 3 s.
cues: Pull the handles to your chest
Push the pad down with your knees
homeSwap: Dumbbell pullover on the floor (lengthened lats) + one-arm DB row with the elbow driving toward the hip to bias lats.
note: Treat this as a bridge to bodyweight pull-ups: track the assistance number in the log, the win is that number dropping.

name: Band-Assisted Pull-Up
doThisNotThat: Use the band for reps at the bottom, but finish the set with negatives so you train the full range unassisted.
steps: Loop a band over the bar and put one knee or both feet in it.
Dead hang, shoulders down.
Pull chin over the bar.
Lower in 3 s; band helps most at the bottom, so own the top.
cues: Pull the bar to your chest
homeSwap: Dumbbell pullover on the floor (lengthened lats) + one-arm DB row with the elbow driving toward the hip to bias lats.
note: Bands help most where you are already strongest (the bottom), so pair with negatives to build the top range.

name: Negative Pull-Up
doThisNotThat: Jump to the top and lower for 4-5 s; don't drop the last third, which is exactly the range you need.
steps: Stand on a box so your chin is at bar height.
Grip overhand, step off with the chin over the bar.
Lower for 4-5 s to a full dead hang.
Step back up and repeat; 3-5 reps per set.
cues: Hold the bar at your chest as long as you can
Lower like an elevator, not a trapdoor
homeSwap: Dumbbell pullover on the floor (lengthened lats) + one-arm DB row with the elbow driving toward the hip to bias lats.
note: Eccentrics build pulling strength fastest for a beginner, but they make you sore: avoid them within 48 h of a fight or game.

name: L-Sit Pull-Up
doThisNotThat: Hold legs straight at hip height the whole rep; letting them drop turns it into a normal pull-up with extra fatigue.
steps: Dead hang, shoulders set down.
Lift straight legs to hip height (bend knees if needed).
Pull chin over the bar without legs dropping.
Lower in 2-3 s.
cues: Point your toes at the wall in front
Pull the bar to your chest
homeSwap: Dumbbell pullover on the floor (lengthened lats) + one-arm DB row with the elbow driving toward the hip to bias lats.
note: Trains the hollow-body position that ties lats to abs, the same link that keeps posture in a grappling scramble.

name: Chin-Up
doThisNotThat: Keep shoulders down at the bottom; don't turn chin-ups into a neck-craning reach for the bar.
steps: Grip underhand, shoulder width.
Dead hang, then pull shoulders down.
Pull until the chin clears the bar, chest toward the bar.
Lower in 2-3 s to full hang.
cues: Pull your elbows down to your ribs
Bring your chest to the bar
homeSwap: Dumbbell pullover on the floor (lengthened lats) + one-arm DB row with the elbow driving toward the hip to bias lats.
note: Underhand puts the biceps in a strong line, so most people get 1-3 more reps: good for arm size, and great for clinch and collar-tie strength.

name: Scapular Pull-Up
doThisNotThat: Move only the shoulder blades, arms stay straight; it is a 2-inch movement, not a half pull-up.
steps: Dead hang, overhand grip.
Keeping elbows straight, pull the shoulders down away from the ears.
Pause 2 s, then let the shoulders rise slowly to full hang.
Do 8-12 slow reps.
cues: Push the bar toward your feet
homeSwap: Prone Y-T-W raises on the floor or a bench, 2-5 lb dumbbells or thumbs up with no weight.
note: Fixes the "shrugged-up" posture and protects the shoulder for punching volume; a perfect warm-up set before pull-ups.

name: Lat Pulldown
doThisNotThat: Pull the bar to the upper chest with a slight lean back, not behind the neck and not with a big swing.
steps: Set the thigh pad so your legs are locked under it.
Grip ~1.5x shoulder width overhand.
Lean back ~10-15°, chest up.
Pull the bar to the top of the chest, pause 1 s, let it rise over 2-3 s until the arms are fully long.
cues: Pull the bar to your collarbones
Drive your elbows into your back pockets
homeSwap: Dumbbell pullover on the floor (lengthened lats) + one-arm DB row with the elbow driving toward the hip to bias lats.
note: Let the bar rise all the way so the lats get a full stretch; the lengthened end of the range is where stretch-loaded growth happens and where your stiff shoulders gain range.
hardestPoint: Bottom 3 inches (bar near the chest), where the lats are shortest.

name: Close-Grip Lat Pulldown
doThisNotThat: Use the V-bar and pull to the sternum with elbows driving down and back, not just bending the arms.
steps: Attach a V-bar handle; lock thighs under the pad.
Start with arms long and lats stretched.
Lean back slightly and pull the handle to the bottom of the chest.
Pause, then return over 2-3 s.
cues: Pull the handle to your sternum
homeSwap: Dumbbell pullover on the floor (lengthened lats) + one-arm DB row with the elbow driving toward the hip to bias lats.
note: Close grip gives a longer range of motion for the lower lats, the part that makes the waist look narrow from behind.

name: Neutral-Grip Lat Pulldown
doThisNotThat: Choose the wide neutral handles if overhand bothers your elbows; same lats, friendlier joints.
steps: Attach wide neutral handles; lock in.
Arms long, shoulders up in a stretch.
Pull handles to the upper chest, elbows by the ribs.
Return over 2-3 s.
cues: Pull your elbows into your sides
homeSwap: Dumbbell pullover on the floor (lengthened lats) + one-arm DB row with the elbow driving toward the hip to bias lats.
note: Matches the hand angle of a body-lock and collar tie; strong here means you control the clinch instead of getting pulled around.

name: Underhand Lat Pulldown
doThisNotThat: Keep the elbows in front of the body and pull to the lower chest; it biases lower lats, not just biceps.
steps: Grip underhand at shoulder width.
Lock thighs under the pad, arms long.
Pull to the lower chest, slight lean back.
Return slowly to full stretch.
cues: Pull your elbows to your hips
homeSwap: Dumbbell pullover on the floor (lengthened lats) + one-arm DB row with the elbow driving toward the hip to bias lats.
note: A good chin-up builder when you can't yet do bodyweight reps; track load until it's about 80% of your bodyweight.

name: Single-Arm Lat Pulldown
doThisNotThat: Let the working shoulder rise into a full stretch at the top, then pull the elbow down to the hip; one side at a time doubles your focus.
steps: Attach a D-handle to the high pulley; sit or kneel facing it.
Reach up so the lat is stretched.
Pull the elbow down toward the hip, slight lean toward the working side.
Return over 2-3 s to full stretch.
cues: Drive your elbow into your back pocket
Pull the handle to your armpit
homeSwap: One-arm dumbbell row with the elbow driving toward the hip.
note: Unilateral work evens out side-to-side differences; boxers usually have a stronger rear-hand side, and this exposes it.

name: Kneeling Cable Pulldown
doThisNotThat: Kneel tall with glutes squeezed so the ribs stay down; arching the low back to finish the rep turns it into a shrug.
steps: Set a rope or bar on the high pulley; kneel tall a step back.
Squeeze glutes, ribs down, arms long overhead.
Pull to the upper chest without leaning back.
Return over 2-3 s.
cues: Pull the rope to your chest
Stay tall like a wall behind you
homeSwap: Dumbbell pullover on the floor (lengthened lats) + one-arm DB row with the elbow driving toward the hip to bias lats.
note: Teaches lats and abs to work together with no leg brace, the same brace you need when pummeling for underhooks.

name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
doThisNotThat: Keep the arms nearly straight and hinge slightly; bending the elbows turns it into a triceps pushdown.
steps: Set a rope or straight bar on the high pulley; step back 2 steps.
Hinge ~20°, arms straight overhead with a slight elbow bend.
Sweep the bar down in an arc to the thighs.
Return over 2-3 s until the lats are stretched.
cues: Sweep the bar to your thighs
Push the floor away through tripod feet
homeSwap: Dumbbell pullover on the floor (lengthened lats) + one-arm DB row with the elbow driving toward the hip to bias lats.
note: Isolates the lats with no biceps help, which teaches you to feel lats before pull-ups; the same arc as a sprawl's arm drive.

name: Dumbbell Pullover
doThisNotThat: Stop when the arms reach ear level with ribs down; flaring the ribs to get deeper only stretches the low back.
steps: Lie across or along a bench, one dumbbell held vertically by the inner plate.
Arms over the chest, slight elbow bend.
Lower the dumbbell behind the head in 3 s until upper arms are by the ears.
Pull it back over the chest.
cues: Pull the dumbbell over in a rainbow
Keep your ribs pinned to the bench
homeSwap: Same exercise on the floor with a light dumbbell; the floor stops you from over-arching.
note: A loaded stretch for lats and chest that opens a stiff thoracic spine; breathe out as you pull to keep ribs down (good habit with asthma).

name: Cable Pullover
doThisNotThat: Use the cable to keep tension at the stretched position, where a dumbbell pullover goes light.
steps: Lie on a bench with your head toward a low pulley, rope or bar in hand.
Arms straight overhead in a stretch.
Pull to over the chest.
Return over 3 s to full stretch.
cues: Pull the rope to your chest in an arc
homeSwap: Dumbbell pullover on the floor.
note: Constant tension at long muscle length; good finisher for lats when your grip is fried from rows.

name: Barbell Row
doThisNotThat: Hinge to ~45° and keep the torso still; standing up more each rep turns it into a shrug.
steps: Grip just outside shoulder width, overhand.
Hinge to ~45°, knees soft, bar hanging below the shoulders.
Brace, then row to the lower ribs.
Lower in 2 s to straight arms without the torso moving.
cues: Pull the bar to your belt
Screw your feet into the floor
homeSwap: One-arm dumbbell row braced on a chair, 3 s lowering, 1 s squeeze; or towel row under a sturdy table (feet planted, body straight).
note: The hinge hold builds the same static back strength you use holding a wrestling stance; brace with a big exhale on each pull.

name: Pendlay Row
doThisNotThat: Reset the bar on the floor every rep and pull explosively; it is a power row, not a slow grind.
steps: Bar on the floor; hinge until torso is near parallel.
Grip just outside shoulder width.
Rip the bar to the lower chest.
Return it to the floor, reset, repeat.
cues: Snap the bar to your sternum
homeSwap: One-arm dumbbell row braced on a chair, 3 s lowering, 1 s squeeze; or towel row under a sturdy table (feet planted, body straight).
note: Dead-stop reps train rate of force development in the upper back; great before boxing because they are fast but low-fatigue.

name: Yates Row
doThisNotThat: Use an underhand grip and ~70° torso angle; don't let it become an upright jerk with the hips.
steps: Underhand grip at shoulder width.
Hinge to ~70°, knees soft.
Row to the belly button, elbows tight.
Lower under control.
cues: Pull the bar to your belly button
homeSwap: One-arm dumbbell row braced on a chair, 3 s lowering, 1 s squeeze; or towel row under a sturdy table (feet planted, body straight).
note: More upright = more load and more lower lats; keep it honest by stopping when rep speed drops.

name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
doThisNotThat: Row the elbow toward the hip in an arc, not straight up toward the ceiling.
steps: Left hand and knee on a bench, right foot planted wide.
Dumbbell hanging, shoulder stretched toward the floor.
Row the elbow toward the hip.
Lower in 2-3 s to a full stretch.
cues: Pull your elbow to your back pocket
Push the bench away with your support hand
homeSwap: Same exercise with a chair and your heaviest dumbbell; add a 2 s pause at the top and a 3 s lowering.
note: Your best home back builder; at the bottom let the shoulder blade slide forward for the stretch, then pull it back first. This is the shoulder blade motion behind a strong jab retraction.

name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
doThisNotThat: Let the bench hold your body so 100% of the effort goes to the back; no hip swing possible.
steps: Set a bench to ~30°; lie face down with chest at the top.
Dumbbells hanging straight down.
Row both elbows back to the ribs.
Lower in 2-3 s.
cues: Pull the dumbbells to your hips
Keep your chest glued to the pad
homeSwap: One-arm dumbbell row braced on a chair, 3 s lowering, 1 s squeeze; or towel row under a sturdy table (feet planted, body straight).
note: Removes low-back fatigue, so it is the row to use on a leg-heavy week or when the back is tired from wrestling.

name: Seal Row
doThisNotThat: Lie flat on a high bench so the legs can't help; pure back.
steps: Lie face down on a raised flat bench.
Grab a barbell or dumbbells below.
Row to the bench underside.
Lower to a full stretch.
cues: Pull the bar to the bench
homeSwap: One-arm dumbbell row braced on a chair, 3 s lowering, 1 s squeeze; or towel row under a sturdy table (feet planted, body straight).
note: Zero cheating means lower loads; track reps and pauses as the progression, not weight jumps.

name: T-Bar Row
doThisNotThat: Use a close neutral grip and row to the chest with a fixed hinge; don't stand up as you pull.
steps: Straddle the bar, hinge to ~45°, V-handle under the plates.
Brace, arms long.
Row to the lower chest.
Lower 2 s.
cues: Pull the handle to your chest
homeSwap: One-arm dumbbell row braced on a chair, 3 s lowering, 1 s squeeze; or towel row under a sturdy table (feet planted, body straight).
note: Lets you load heavy with a neutral grip that matches the clinch; great mid-back thickness builder.

name: Meadows Row
doThisNotThat: Stand perpendicular to the bar and row the end with an overhand grip; the angle stretches the upper lats.
steps: Bar end in a landmine; stand perpendicular to it.
Staggered stance, hinge, grip the thick end overhand.
Row the elbow up and back.
Lower to a full stretch.
cues: Pull your elbow past your hip
Push the ground away with the front foot
homeSwap: One-arm dumbbell row braced on a chair, 3 s lowering, 1 s squeeze; or towel row under a sturdy table (feet planted, body straight).
note: Staggered stance plus a single arm mimics a rear-hand pull in a clinch; train both sides evenly.

name: Seated Cable Row
doThisNotThat: Let the shoulders reach forward at the start for the stretch, then row; keeping them pinned the whole time cuts the range.
steps: Sit with feet on the platform, knees soft, V-handle in hand.
Torso upright, arms long, shoulders reaching forward.
Row to the belly, elbows tight.
Return 2-3 s, letting the shoulder blades slide forward.
cues: Pull the handle to your belly button
Push your feet into the platform
homeSwap: One-arm dumbbell row braced on a chair, 3 s lowering, 1 s squeeze; or towel row under a sturdy table (feet planted, body straight).
note: Torso stays near vertical; a 10° lean is fine, rocking 30° is momentum. Exhale as you pull.

name: Wide-Grip Cable Row
doThisNotThat: Elbows flare ~60° and pull to the lower chest to bias upper back and rear delts.
steps: Attach a straight bar, grip wide.
Sit tall, arms long.
Row to the lower chest with elbows out.
Return slowly.
cues: Pull the bar to your chest
homeSwap: Prone Y-T-W raises on the floor or a bench, 2-5 lb dumbbells or thumbs up with no weight.
note: Upper back and rear delts build the posture that counters a slouched, forward-shoulder look.

name: Single-Arm Cable Row
doThisNotThat: Let the torso rotate a little toward the cable at the stretch, then turn back as you row; this trains the full chain.
steps: Set a handle at chest height; split stance.
Reach forward, letting the shoulder blade wrap around.
Row and rotate back to square.
Return slowly.
homeSwap: One-arm dumbbell row braced on a chair, 3 s lowering, 1 s squeeze; or towel row under a sturdy table (feet planted, body straight).
note: The rotation-to-square pattern is the reverse of a cross; it trains the deceleration side of punching.

name: Machine Row
doThisNotThat: Set the seat so the handles line up with your lower chest; too low and it becomes a shrug.
steps: Adjust seat so handles are at lower-chest height.
Chest on the pad.
Row elbows back.
Return to full stretch.
cues: Pull the handles to your ribs
homeSwap: One-arm dumbbell row braced on a chair, 3 s lowering, 1 s squeeze; or towel row under a sturdy table (feet planted, body straight).
note: Easy to push close to failure safely; take the last set to failure with lengthened partials.

name: Kroc Row
doThisNotThat: Heavy dumbbell, 15-20 reps, a little body English allowed, but the lowering stays controlled.
steps: One hand on a bench, staggered stance.
Heaviest dumbbell you can row for 15+.
Row explosively; slight torso rotation okay.
Lower under control.
cues: Rip the dumbbell to your hip
homeSwap: One-arm dumbbell row braced on a chair, 3 s lowering, 1 s squeeze; or towel row under a sturdy table (feet planted, body straight).
note: High-rep heavy rows build grip endurance for grappling; use as a once-a-week finisher, not every session.

name: Inverted Row
doThisNotThat: Keep the body in one plank line from heels to head; sagging hips cut the load.
steps: Set a bar at waist height (or lie under a sturdy table).
Hang under it, heels on the floor, body straight.
Pull the chest to the bar.
Lower in 2-3 s.
cues: Pull your chest to the bar
Squeeze your glutes like a plank
homeSwap: Lie under a sturdy table, grip the edge, and row your chest up to it; elevate your feet to make it harder.
note: At home this is your best horizontal pull; feet elevated plus a 2 s pause at the top progresses it for months.

name: Ring Row
doThisNotThat: Let the hands turn naturally from palms-down to palms-in as you pull; the rings let the shoulders move freely.
steps: Set rings or straps at chest height.
Walk feet forward, body straight.
Row hands to the ribs.
Lower slowly.
cues: Pull the rings to your ribs
homeSwap: Towel row under a sturdy table.
note: Unstable handles force the shoulder stabilizers to work, good for punch-heavy shoulders.

name: Renegade Row
doThisNotThat: Feet wide and hips square; the win is a still torso, not a heavy row.
steps: Plank on two dumbbells, feet wider than hips.
Brace, push one dumbbell into the floor.
Row the other to the hip without the hips rotating.
Alternate sides.
cues: Push the floor away with the bottom hand
Keep your belt buckle facing the floor
homeSwap: Same move on the floor with bodyweight; slow the tempo to 3 s each way to make it harder.
note: An anti-rotation drill as much as a row; it builds the stiff trunk that stops you getting turned in the clinch.

name: Gorilla Row
doThisNotThat: Wide deep hinge, alternating rows, with the non-rowing hand pressing down into its bell.
steps: Two kettlebells between the feet, wide stance.
Hinge low, grip both handles.
Row one while pressing the other down.
Alternate sides.
cues: Push one bell into the floor as you pull the other
homeSwap: One-arm dumbbell row braced on a chair, 3 s lowering, 1 s squeeze; or towel row under a sturdy table (feet planted, body straight).
note: Alternating push-pull through the trunk is the same rhythm as hand-fighting.

name: Face Pull
doThisNotThat: Pull the rope to your forehead and spread the hands apart; finish with thumbs pointing back.
steps: Rope on a pulley at forehead height.
Step back, arms long.
Pull to the forehead, hands spreading to ear level.
Return slowly.
cues: Pull the rope apart to your ears
Show your biceps to the wall
homeSwap: Prone Y-T-W raises on the floor or a bench, 2-5 lb dumbbells or thumbs up with no weight.
note: Balances all the pressing and punching; 2-3 sets weekly is cheap shoulder insurance for a boxer.

name: Bent-Over Dumbbell Rear Delt Fly
doThisNotThat: Lead with the pinkies and keep a slight elbow bend; heaving heavy weights turns it into a row.
steps: Light dumbbells; hinge to ~70°.
Arms hanging, slight elbow bend.
Sweep arms out to the sides.
Lower in 2 s.
cues: Throw the dumbbells to the walls
homeSwap: Same exercise with your light home dumbbells; add a 1 s pause at the top.
note: Rear delts round out the shoulder for the "3D" look, and they decelerate the arm after every punch.

name: Cable Rear Delt Fly
doThisNotThat: Cross the cables (left hand takes the right cable) at shoulder height for a longer stretch.
steps: Set two pulleys at shoulder height.
Cross arms to grab opposite cables.
Sweep arms out wide.
Return slowly to crossed.
cues: Sweep your hands to the walls
homeSwap: Prone Y-T-W raises on the floor or a bench, 2-5 lb dumbbells or thumbs up with no weight.
note: Constant tension through a long range; the crossed start stretches the rear delt.

name: Reverse Pec Deck
doThisNotThat: Set the handles so arms start forward, and lead with the elbows, not the hands.
steps: Face the pad, chest on it.
Handles at shoulder height.
Sweep arms back to in line with the body.
Return slowly.
cues: Push the handles to the walls
homeSwap: Prone Y-T-W raises on the floor or a bench, 2-5 lb dumbbells or thumbs up with no weight.
note: Easy to take to failure safely: last set to failure plus partials in the stretched (front) position.

name: Chest-Supported Rear Delt Raise
doThisNotThat: Chest on an incline bench removes momentum completely.
steps: Incline bench ~30°, lie face down.
Light dumbbells hanging.
Raise arms out to the sides.
Lower slowly.
cues: Spread the dumbbells to the walls
homeSwap: Prone Y-T-W raises on the floor or a bench, 2-5 lb dumbbells or thumbs up with no weight.
note: Pure rear delt with no lower-back fatigue; a good accessory after heavy legs.

name: Band Pull-Apart
doThisNotThat: Keep arms straight at shoulder height and pull until the band touches the chest.
steps: Hold a light band at shoulder width, arms straight in front.
Stand tall.
Pull the band apart to the chest.
Return slowly.
cues: Stretch the band to your chest
homeSwap: Prone Y-T-W raises on the floor or a bench, 2-5 lb dumbbells or thumbs up with no weight.
note: High-rep, low-fatigue posture work; 2 sets of 20 between rounds of shadowboxing keeps the shoulders healthy.

name: Prone Y-T-W Raise
doThisNotThat: Thumbs up and arms long; tiny weights or none, perfect shape beats heavy.
steps: Lie face down on the floor or an incline bench.
Raise arms into a Y, hold 2 s.
Then a T, hold 2 s.
Then a W, hold 2 s.
cues: Reach your thumbs to the ceiling
homeSwap: Prone Y-T-W raises on the floor or a bench, 2-5 lb dumbbells or thumbs up with no weight.
note: Lower traps fix the shrugged shoulder posture; do these on rest days too.

name: Barbell Shrug
doThisNotThat: Shrug straight up toward the ears and pause; rolling the shoulders adds nothing.
steps: Hold the bar at hip height, shoulder width.
Stand tall, tripod feet.
Shrug up, pause 1-2 s.
Lower slowly to a full stretch.
cues: Lift your shoulders to your ears
homeSwap: Dumbbell shrug with your heaviest pair, 2 s pause at the top.
note: Big traps protect the neck in boxing and grappling; pair shrugs with neck work.

name: Dumbbell Shrug
doThisNotThat: Hold the pause at the top for 2 s every rep.
steps: Dumbbells at the sides.
Stand tall.
Shrug up, pause.
Lower to full stretch.
cues: Lift your shoulders to your ears
homeSwap: Same at home; slow the lowering to 3 s.
note: Neck and trap mass is part of a fighter's look and protection.

name: Trap Bar Shrug
doThisNotThat: The neutral grip lets you load heavy without the bar dragging on your thighs.
steps: Stand in the trap bar, grip the handles.
Lift to standing.
Shrug and pause.
Lower slowly.
cues: Lift your shoulders to your ears
homeSwap: Dumbbell shrug.
note: Easiest heavy shrug on the back; good when the low back is tired.

name: Cable Shrug
doThisNotThat: Constant tension at the bottom stretch.
steps: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley; stand close to the stack.
Grip shoulder width, arms long.
Shrug straight up and pause 1-2 s.
Lower to a full stretch.
cues: Lift your shoulders to your ears
homeSwap: Dumbbell shrug.
note: Constant tension at the bottom stretch where dumbbells go light; good for high-rep trap and neck-protection work after heavy pulls.

name: Barbell High Pull
doThisNotThat: Explode with the hips and let the elbows ride high; it is a jump with the arms following, not an upright row.
steps: Bar at mid-thigh (hang position).
Dip a few inches with a vertical torso.
Drive hips and legs through like a jump.
Let the elbows pull high and out; bar to the chest.
homeSwap: Dumbbell high pull from the hang with the same jump.
note: Ground → hips → traps → arms sequencing is the exact firing order your arm-first habit needs; light and fast.

name: Front Plank
doThisNotThat: Squeeze glutes and pull elbows toward toes; long sloppy holds teach nothing.
steps: Forearms on the floor, elbows under shoulders.
Legs straight, feet hip width.
Squeeze glutes, ribs down.
Breathe in short nasal breaths; hold 20-30 s.
cues: Pull your elbows to your toes
homeSwap: Same move on the floor with bodyweight; slow the tempo to 3 s each way to make it harder.
note: Short, maximal-tension holds (20-30 s) build more trunk stiffness than 2-minute holds; exhale-focused breathing keeps the brace without breath-holding.

name: RKC Plank
doThisNotThat: Maximum full-body tension for 10-15 s, not a long relaxed hold.
steps: Forearm plank, elbows slightly ahead of shoulders.
Squeeze glutes and quads hard.
Drag elbows toward toes without moving.
Hold 10-15 s.
cues: Pull your elbows to your toes
homeSwap: Same move on the floor with bodyweight; slow the tempo to 3 s each way to make it harder.
note: Teaches the full-body tension you need to absorb a body shot or a takedown attempt.

name: Side Plank
doThisNotThat: Stack shoulder over elbow and push hips forward; sagging hips just hang off the joints.
steps: Elbow under shoulder, legs stacked or staggered.
Lift hips to a straight line.
Push top hip forward slightly.
Hold 20-30 s each side.
cues: Lift your top hip to the ceiling
homeSwap: Same move on the floor with bodyweight; slow the tempo to 3 s each way to make it harder.
note: Lateral trunk stiffness transfers to stance and to resisting being bent sideways in the clinch.

name: Side Plank with Leg Lift
doThisNotThat: Lift the top leg slowly without the hips dropping or rotating.
steps: Side plank on elbow.
Lift top leg 12 inches.
Hold 2 s, lower.
6-10 lifts per side.
cues: Kick the top heel to the wall
homeSwap: Same move on the floor with bodyweight; slow the tempo to 3 s each way to make it harder.
note: Glute medius control here helps stop the knee from caving, which flat feet push toward.

name: Dead Bug
doThisNotThat: Keep the low back pressed down; if it lifts, shorten the range.
steps: Lie on your back, arms to the ceiling, knees over hips.
Exhale fully, press low back into the floor.
Lower opposite arm and leg slowly.
Return and switch.
cues: Push your low back into the floor
homeSwap: Same move on the floor with bodyweight; slow the tempo to 3 s each way to make it harder.
note: Long exhales during dead bugs train the diaphragm and brace together; useful breathing practice with asthma.

name: Bird Dog
doThisNotThat: Move slow enough that a cup on your back would not spill.
steps: Hands under shoulders, knees under hips.
Reach one arm and the opposite leg long.
Hold 2 s.
Return and switch.
cues: Reach your heel to the wall behind
Keep your back flat like a table
homeSwap: Same move on the floor with bodyweight; slow the tempo to 3 s each way to make it harder.
note: Cross-body coordination drill, good for your sequencing and balance work.

name: Hollow Body Hold
doThisNotThat: Low back flat on the floor; raise legs higher if it lifts.
steps: Lie on your back, arms overhead.
Press low back down, lift shoulders and legs.
Hold 20-30 s or rock gently.
Bend knees to make it easier.
cues: Push your low back into the floor
homeSwap: Same move on the floor with bodyweight; slow the tempo to 3 s each way to make it harder.
note: The hollow position is the base for gymnastics and for the L-sit pull-up.

name: Ab Wheel Rollout
doThisNotThat: Roll only as far as you can keep a flat back; sagging hips load the spine, not the abs.
steps: Kneel, wheel under shoulders.
Brace and squeeze glutes.
Roll forward slowly.
Pull back with the arms and abs together.
cues: Push the wheel away with your arms
homeSwap: Floor slider or towel rollout on a smooth floor.
note: One of the strongest anti-extension exercises; protects the low back in sprawls.

name: Standing Ab Wheel Rollout
doThisNotThat: Advanced only: master full kneeling rollouts first.
steps: Stand, hinge and place the wheel on the floor in front of the feet.
Brace hard, squeeze glutes, tuck the pelvis.
Roll out only as far as you can keep a flat back (start with a wall stopping the wheel).
Pull back to standing with arms and abs together.
homeSwap: Kneeling rollout with a pause.
note: Only after 10+ clean full kneeling rollouts; use a wall to limit the range and move the wall back an inch a week.

name: Stability Ball Rollout
doThisNotThat: Roll only until the arms are overhead with hips still tucked; the ball makes the rollout easier than a wheel, so use it to learn the shape.
steps: Kneel facing a stability ball, forearms on top, fists together.
Squeeze glutes and tuck the pelvis slightly.
Roll the ball forward until hips and shoulders form a line.
Pull it back with the forearms and abs, exhaling.
cues: Push the ball away with your forearms
homeSwap: Kneeling ab wheel or plank.
note: The easiest anti-extension progression before the ab wheel; sets of 8-10 slow reps build the brace you need to stay stiff when a body shot lands.

name: Stir the Pot
doThisNotThat: Draw small slow circles with the forearms while hips and ribs stay totally still; big fast circles let the trunk wobble.
steps: Forearm plank on a stability ball, feet wide.
Squeeze glutes, ribs down.
Draw 5 small circles clockwise with the forearms.
Then 5 counterclockwise; rest.
cues: Draw small circles with your elbows
homeSwap: Plank with shoulder taps.
note: Unstable anti-extension trains the reflexive trunk stiffness that keeps you square when someone pushes or pulls you off balance.

name: Pallof Press
doThisNotThat: Press straight out and hold; the cable tries to rotate you, your job is to not move.
steps: Cable or band at chest height; stand side-on.
Handle at chest, feet hip width.
Press straight out, hold 2 s.
Return; 8-12 reps per side.
cues: Screw your feet into the floor
homeSwap: Plank shoulder taps or a single-arm DB farmer hold.
note: Anti-rotation stiffness is what lets hip rotation reach the fist instead of leaking out of the trunk.

name: Pallof Walkout
doThisNotThat: Walk sideways with arms extended; don't let the cable pull you around.
steps: Cable or band at chest height; hold the handle at your sternum and press arms straight.
Stand side-on in an athletic stance: knees ~25°, tripod feet.
Side-step away from the anchor 3-4 steps with arms locked out.
Hold 2 s, then step back in; 4-6 trips per side.
cues: Keep your hands on your center line
Push the floor sideways with each step
homeSwap: Suitcase carry.
note: Combines footwork with a braced trunk, like circling the ring while staying square to the opponent.

name: Overhead Pallof Press
doThisNotThat: Press overhead without arching the low back.
steps: Stand side-on to a chest-height cable or band.
Hold the handle at your sternum, feet hip width, glutes on.
Press the handle straight overhead without the ribs flaring.
Hold 2 s, lower; 8 per side.
cues: Reach the handle to the ceiling
homeSwap: Plank shoulder taps.
note: Adds shoulder stability to anti-rotation; useful for volleyball and tennis overhead positions where the trunk must stay stacked.

name: Half-Kneeling Cable Chop
doThisNotThat: Turn from the hips with the arms following, not a pull with the arms.
steps: Half kneel, inside knee down, rope on a high pulley.
Rope over the far shoulder.
Pull across and down past the far hip.
Return slowly.
cues: Pull the rope to your far hip
homeSwap: Dumbbell woodchop from half kneeling.
note: Teaches hips-lead rotation, the same order you need in a hook or rear hand.

name: Half-Kneeling Cable Lift
doThisNotThat: Push and pull the rope up across the body; the trunk stays tall.
steps: Half kneel with the inside knee down, rope on a low pulley beside you.
Grip the rope at the near hip, tall torso.
Pull the rope to the chest, then press it up and across to the far shoulder.
Return slowly; 8-10 per side.
cues: Push the rope to the far ceiling
homeSwap: Dumbbell lift from half kneeling.
note: Low-to-high mirrors an uppercut or a golf/tennis follow-through; the trunk transfers force from the hip without bending.

name: Cable Woodchop
doThisNotThat: Pivot the back foot and drive the hips; the arms are just ropes.
steps: Cable high, stand side-on.
Rotate from the hips, pivoting back foot.
Finish facing away.
Return slowly.
cues: Throw the rope past your hip
homeSwap: Dumbbell woodchop.
note: The back-foot pivot is the same pivot as a power punch.

name: Dumbbell Woodchop
doThisNotThat: Pivot and let the hips start.
steps: Hold one dumbbell with both hands outside one shoulder, feet shoulder width.
Rotate the hips first and chop the dumbbell down across to the opposite knee.
Pivot the back foot as you turn.
Return under control; 8-10 per side.
cues: Chop the dumbbell past your knee
homeSwap: Same at home with a light dumbbell.
note: Your home rotational drill: keep it light and fast, the goal is hips first, arms last, the fix for your arm-first sequencing.

name: Landmine Rotation
doThisNotThat: Move the bar in a rainbow with the hips driving and arms almost straight.
steps: Hold the bar end with both hands at eye level.
Pivot feet and rotate the bar to one hip.
Drive back to the other side.
Keep arms long.
cues: Draw a rainbow with the bar
homeSwap: Dumbbell woodchop.
note: Great rotational strength drill for punching.

name: Russian Twist
doThisNotThat: Rotate the ribcage, not just the arms; better yet, choose Pallof press or chops for punch transfer.
steps: Sit, lean back ~45° with a straight back.
Feet down (easier) or up (harder).
Rotate the ribcage to touch the floor beside each hip.
Exhale on each turn.
cues: Turn your chest to each wall
homeSwap: Same move on the floor with bodyweight; slow the tempo to 3 s each way to make it harder.
note: Weak transfer to punching versus standing anti-rotation and chops; keep it as an accessory, not the main core work.

name: Hanging Knee Raise
doThisNotThat: Curl the pelvis up, don't just lift the knees.
steps: Hang from a bar, shoulders pulled down.
Bring the knees up toward the chest.
Curl the pelvis up at the top so the low back rounds slightly.
Lower in 2-3 s without swinging.
cues: Bring your knees to your chest
homeSwap: Lying reverse crunch.
note: Curling the pelvis (not just lifting the knees) is what works the abs; hanging also builds grip for grappling and decompresses the spine.

name: Hanging Leg Raise
doThisNotThat: Straight legs, no swing.
steps: Hang with shoulders set down, legs straight.
Lift straight legs to hip height or higher.
Curl the pelvis at the top.
Lower in 2-3 s, no swing.
cues: Lift your toes to the bar
homeSwap: Lying leg raise.
note: Strong lower abs and hip flexors help you absorb body shots and lift the knees for checks and knees in MMA.

name: Toes-to-Bar
doThisNotThat: Strict toes to bar with no kipping.
steps: Hang from the bar, shoulders set.
Press the bar down toward your hips with straight arms.
Lift the legs and touch the toes to the bar.
Lower slowly; no kipping.
cues: Touch the bar with your toes
homeSwap: V-up.
note: Lats push the bar down while the abs curl; advanced, so build hanging leg raises to 10 clean reps first.

name: Captain's Chair Knee Raise
doThisNotThat: Curl the hips up off the pad.
steps: Back flat on the pad, forearms on the rests.
Let the legs hang straight.
Raise the knees and curl the hips off the pad.
Lower slowly.
cues: Bring your knees to your chest
homeSwap: Lying reverse crunch.
note: A supported version of the hanging knee raise when grip is tired; still curl the pelvis, not just the knees.

name: Lying Leg Raise
doThisNotThat: Keep low back pressed down.
steps: Lie on your back, hands under the hips.
Press the low back into the floor.
Raise straight legs to 90°.
Lower slowly, stopping where the low back lifts.
cues: Push your low back into the floor
Lift your toes to the ceiling
homeSwap: Same move on the floor with bodyweight; slow the tempo to 3 s each way to make it harder.
note: Stop the lowering where the back peels off the floor; that point moves lower as you get stronger, track it.

name: Reverse Crunch
doThisNotThat: Curl hips off the floor.
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent at 90°, hands by the hips.
Exhale and curl the knees toward the chest, lifting the hips.
Pause 1 s.
Lower slowly.
cues: Curl your hips to your ribs
homeSwap: Same move on the floor with bodyweight; slow the tempo to 3 s each way to make it harder.
note: Lower-ab emphasis with less hip flexor than leg raises; a long exhale at the top trains the breathing brace.

name: Cable Crunch
doThisNotThat: Curl the spine; don't just bend at the hips.
steps: Kneel facing a high pulley, rope held at the sides of the head.
Hips stay still and high.
Curl the ribs down toward the hips, elbows to the knees.
Return slowly to a stretch.
cues: Curl your ribs to your hips
homeSwap: Crunch with a pause.
note: Loadable ab hypertrophy: progress weight like any lift, 8-15 reps, last set to failure; visible abs need muscle plus staying lean (not dieting).

name: Crunch
doThisNotThat: Curl only the upper back off the floor; exhale fully at the top.
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent, hands across the chest.
Exhale fully and curl the shoulder blades off the floor.
Pause 1 s at the top.
Lower slowly.
cues: Curl your ribs to your hips
homeSwap: Same move on the floor with bodyweight; slow the tempo to 3 s each way to make it harder.
note: Full exhale at the top doubles as breathing practice.

name: Sit-Up
doThisNotThat: Controlled, no yanking the neck.
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat.
Arms across the chest.
Curl up to sitting, chin tucked.
Lower slowly.
cues: Curl your chest to your knees
homeSwap: Same move on the floor with bodyweight; slow the tempo to 3 s each way to make it harder.
note: Fine for abs, but crunches, rollouts and anti-rotation work cover more; don't yank the neck.

name: Decline Sit-Up
doThisNotThat: Controlled lowering.
steps: Hook the feet on a decline bench.
Arms across the chest.
Lower back slowly to just above parallel.
Curl up to upright.
cues: Curl your chest to your knees
homeSwap: Same move on the floor with bodyweight; slow the tempo to 3 s each way to make it harder.
note: Harder sit-up; hold a light plate on the chest to progress. Keep the lowering slow to load the abs, not the hip flexors.

name: V-Up
doThisNotThat: Reach hands to feet at the same time.
steps: Lie flat, arms overhead, legs straight.
Lift arms and legs at the same time.
Touch hands to feet at the top.
Lower slowly.
homeSwap: Same move on the floor with bodyweight; slow the tempo to 3 s each way to make it harder.
note: Coordination and core together; bend knees (tuck-ups) if the back arches on the way down.

name: L-Sit
doThisNotThat: Push down hard and lift legs straight.
steps: Hands on parallettes, dip bars or two sturdy chairs.
Push down hard so the shoulders depress.
Lift the legs straight in front.
Hold 10-20 s; tuck knees to make it easier.
homeSwap: Tuck sit between two chairs.
note: Builds hip flexor, triceps and core strength together; also a great test of how much your stiff hamstrings let you hold straight legs.

name: Dragon Flag
doThisNotThat: Advanced; lower slowly in one line.
steps: Lie on a bench and grip the bench behind your head.
Lift the body to vertical on the upper back.
Lower in a straight line slowly.
Start with eccentric-only reps.
homeSwap: Lying leg raise.
note: Very hard; 3-5 slow negatives beats sloppy full reps. Skip within 48 h of a game.

name: Jefferson Curl
doThisNotThat: Very light weight, slow vertebra-by-vertebra roll.
steps: Stand on a low box with a 5-10 lb weight.
Tuck the chin and roll down one vertebra at a time.
Let the weight go below the box as range allows.
Roll back up slowly, head last.
cues: Roll down one vertebra at a time
homeSwap: Bodyweight Jefferson curl.
note: Light only (5-10 lb): this builds spinal flexion range for an all-over-stiff back, not strength. Stop if anything feels sharp.

name: McGill Curl-Up
doThisNotThat: Tiny range, neutral spine.
steps: Lie on your back, one knee bent, the other leg straight.
Hands under the low back to keep its natural curve.
Lift head and shoulders an inch or two; hold 8-10 s.
Do 5 holds, switch legs.
cues: Lift your chest a few inches
homeSwap: Same move on the floor with bodyweight; slow the tempo to 3 s each way to make it harder.
note: Spine-friendly ab endurance; good on days the back is tired from wrestling.

name: Farmer Carry
doThisNotThat: Walk tall with short, quick, quiet steps; slouching with long strides wastes the drill.
steps: Deadlift two heavy dumbbells or kettlebells to your sides.
Stand tall, shoulders down, ribs stacked over the pelvis.
Walk 20-40 m with short, quick steps.
Set down with a flat back.
cues: Walk tall like a string pulls your head
homeSwap: Same with heavy home dumbbells.
note: Grip, traps and posture in one; also builds the foot stiffness flat feet need, as each step lands on a tripod foot under load.

name: Suitcase Carry
doThisNotThat: Stay perfectly level with one heavy weight; leaning away from it hides the work.
steps: Pick up one heavy dumbbell or kettlebell.
Stand tall, both shoulders level.
Walk 20-30 m with short steps.
Switch hands and repeat.
homeSwap: Same at home.
note: Anti-lateral flexion: the obliques on the empty-hand side work hardest, the same side bend you resist in a clinch.

name: Overhead Carry
doThisNotThat: Lock the arm straight with the biceps by the ear; a bent elbow overhead dumps the load into the low back.
steps: Press one dumbbell or kettlebell overhead.
Lock the elbow, biceps by the ear, ribs down.
Walk 15-30 m.
Lower under control, switch arms.
cues: Reach the weight to the ceiling
homeSwap: Same at home.
note: Shoulder stability for punching and volleyball; if your shoulders are stiff overhead, start light and don't force the lockout.

name: Front-Rack Carry
doThisNotThat: Hold the weights high at the chest with elbows in; letting them sag pulls you into a slouch.
steps: Hold one weight as a goblet or two kettlebells in the rack position.
Elbows in, chest up, ribs down.
Walk 20-30 m.
Set down with control.
cues: Keep the weight on your chest
homeSwap: Same at home.
note: Anti-extension carry that also trains breathing under load: short nasal breaths behind a brace, useful practice with asthma.

name: Waiter Carry
doThisNotThat: Hold the weight overhead palm up like a tray and keep it level.
steps: Hold a kettlebell or dumbbell overhead, palm up like a tray.
Elbow locked, biceps by the ear.
Walk 15-30 m.
Switch arms.
homeSwap: Same at home.
note: Rotator-cuff stability for the shoulders that take all your punching volume.

name: Sandbag Bear-Hug Carry
doThisNotThat: Squeeze the bag high on the chest; letting it slide to the belly rounds the back.
steps: Lift a sandbag (or heavy backpack) and hug it high on the chest.
Lock the hands around it.
Walk 20-40 m.
Set down with a hinge.
cues: Squeeze the bag into your chest
homeSwap: Bear-hug a heavy backpack filled with books.
note: Direct grappling transfer: it is a body lock with a resisting load.

name: Plank Shoulder Tap
doThisNotThat: Feet wider than hips and hips dead still; fast rocking taps miss the point.
steps: High plank, hands under shoulders, feet wide.
Squeeze glutes, ribs down.
Lift one hand to tap the opposite shoulder without the hips moving.
Alternate slowly; 10-20 taps.
cues: Keep your belt buckle facing the floor
homeSwap: Same move on the floor with bodyweight; slow the tempo to 3 s each way to make it harder.
note: Best home anti-rotation drill: narrow the feet to make it harder.

name: Body Saw
doThisNotThat: Push back only as far as the hips stay level.
steps: Forearm plank with feet on sliders or a towel.
Push the body back by moving the forearms.
Pull forward to the start.
8-12 slow reps.
cues: Push the floor forward with your forearms
homeSwap: Towel under the feet on a smooth floor.
note: A home ab-wheel substitute; the longer lever trains the same anti-extension.

name: Hanging Windshield Wiper
doThisNotThat: Control the rotation; don't let the legs swing past where you can stop them.
steps: Hang with legs raised to 90° (bent knees easier).
Rotate the legs to one side.
Stop, pull back through center.
Alternate.
cues: Point your toes to each wall
homeSwap: Lying windshield wiper on the floor.
note: Rotational control for grappling, where you turn the hips while hanging onto an opponent.

name: Turkish Get-Up
doThisNotThat: Light weight, slow, eyes on the bell; speed or heavy loads miss the point.
steps: Lie down, bell pressed up in one hand, same-side knee bent.
Roll to the elbow, then the hand.
Bridge the hips and sweep the leg to a kneel.
Stand up; reverse each step to lie down.
cues: Keep your eyes on the bell
homeSwap: Bodyweight get-up with a shoe balanced on the fist.
note: Builds shoulder stability and the floor-to-standing pattern (technical stand-up) used in MMA and BJJ.

name: Bear Plank Hold
doThisNotThat: Knees hover 1 inch off the floor with back flat.
steps: Hands under shoulders, knees under hips.
Lift knees 1 inch off the floor.
Hold 20-40 s, breathing through the nose.
Add shoulder taps to progress.
cues: Keep a cup balanced on your back
homeSwap: Same move on the floor with bodyweight; slow the tempo to 3 s each way to make it harder.
note: Base for bear crawls and the grappling base position.

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Pullover to Press
doThisNotThat: Keep ribs down through the stretch.
steps: Lie on the floor, dumbbell held over the chest.
Lower it behind the head in 3 s.
Pull back over the chest.
Press to lockout; repeat.
cues: Pull the dumbbell over your chest
homeSwap: Same at home.
note: Combines a lats stretch with a press; good home upper-body finisher.

name: Barbell Bench Press
doThisNotThat: Touch the bar to the lower chest with forearms vertical, not the neck with elbows flared to 90°.
steps: Eyes under the bar, feet flat and slightly behind knees.
Grip ~1.5x shoulder width so forearms are vertical at the bottom.
Pinch shoulder blades down and back, small arch, butt on the bench.
Unrack to over the shoulders, lower 2-3 s to the sternum/nipple line with elbows ~45-60° from the torso.
Drive up and slightly back toward the rack line.
cues: Bend the bar into a U.
Push yourself away from the bar into the bench.
Drive the floor away with your feet.
homeSwap: Deficit push-up between two dumbbells, 3-s lowering, 1-s pause in the stretch; add a backpack when 15+ reps is easy.
note: Leg drive is a ground-up force lesson: screw the feet into the floor before unracking and the press gets a stable base, the same chain you need for a straight punch.
hardestPoint: Just off the chest (longest pec/delt moment arm).

name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
doThisNotThat: Use a 30° bench, not 45°+, so the upper chest does the work instead of the front delts.
steps: Set the bench to 30° (2nd-3rd notch).
Grip slightly narrower than flat bench; forearms vertical at the bottom.
Shoulder blades down and back, chest up to the bar.
Lower to the upper chest just below the collarbones.
Press up and slightly back over the shoulders.
cues: Push the bar toward the ceiling, not the rack.
Keep your chest tall to the bar.
homeSwap: Feet-elevated (decline) push-up on a chair, 3-s lowering; or floor-incline DB press with hips bridged.
note: Upper chest is the V-taper shelf; 30° gives most of the clavicular-head bias without turning it into a shoulder press.

name: Decline Bench Press
doThisNotThat: Use a mild 15-20° decline and touch the lower chest; steeper declines just shorten the range.
steps: Hook feet under the pads, set a 15-20° decline.
Grip ~1.5x shoulder width.
Lower 2-3 s to the bottom of the sternum.
Press straight up over the shoulders.
cues: Push the bar to the ceiling.
homeSwap: Push-up with hands on two dumbbells (neutral height) and feet on floor, 3-s lowering.
note: Shorter range than flat; treat it as a variation for elbows/shoulders that feel cranky on flat, not a main lift.

name: Close-Grip Bench Press
doThisNotThat: Grip at shoulder width, not hands touching; too narrow wrecks the wrists and shortens triceps range.
steps: Grip at shoulder width (index fingers about on the smooth/knurl edge).
Tuck elbows to ~30° from the torso.
Lower 2-3 s to the lower sternum.
Press up, locking out hard.
cues: Drive the bar off your chest like a punch.
homeSwap: Diamond or close-grip push-up, 3-s lowering, feet elevated to add load.
note: Lockout strength is a straight-punch finish; finish every rep with a hard elbow extension.
hardestPoint: Mid-range as triceps take over (~90° elbow).

name: Paused Bench Press
doThisNotThat: Pause 1-2 s on the chest without sinking the bar in; stay tight and press from a dead stop.
steps: Set up like a flat bench.
Lower 2 s, pause 1-2 s motionless on the chest.
Keep shoulder blades pinned and legs tight through the pause.
Press explosively from the pause.
cues: Freeze the bar on your chest.
homeSwap: Paused deficit push-up: 2-s pause 1 inch off the floor.
note: Pauses kill the stretch reflex, so you learn to produce force from zero; useful for the arm-first sequencing problem because you must stay braced.

name: Spoto Press
doThisNotThat: Stop 1-2 inches above the chest and hold 1 s, staying tight; don't let the bar drift toward the face.
steps: Bench setup as normal.
Lower 2-3 s and stop an inch above the chest.
Hold 1 s with lats tight.
Press from the hover.
cues: Hover the bar over your shirt.
homeSwap: Push-up with a 1-s hover one inch off the floor.
note: Builds control in the bottom position where flat feet and loose bracing usually leak force.

name: Larsen Press
doThisNotThat: Feet off the floor and legs straight; it trains upper-body stability, so use ~10-15% less than your bench.
steps: Lie on a flat bench, legs extended and feet hovering.
Grip as normal bench.
Lower 2-3 s to the chest staying centered.
Press without wobbling side to side.
cues: Keep the bar level like a tray.
homeSwap: Floor press with a light DB, legs extended.
note: No leg drive means no hiding; reveals left/right imbalances quickly.
